circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, has been the home of Formula One's season finale since 2009. The venue represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One destination, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track that loops around Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb and holds an FIA Grade 1 license. It serves as the venue for the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix, alongside supporting motorsport events including the Supercars Championship round.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located near Spielberg in Austria's Styria region, this 4. 326 km circuit originally operated as the Österreichring and staged the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following a reconstruction and renaming to the A1-Ring, it returned to hosting the Austrian Grand Prix during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital that stretches 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest venue on the F1 calendar. The circuit hosted its first Formula One race in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before being renamed the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, this 5. 412 km circuit in Bahrain became the first Middle Eastern venue to host a Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track accommodates various motorsport series including GP2 racing, drag racing, and 24-hour endurance competitions, with multiple configuration options available.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, located in Montmeló near Barcelona, spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced layout combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing multiple aspects of car performance. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located near Stavelot in Belgium's Wallonia region, this 7. 004 km circuit has been hosting the Belgian Grand Prix since 1950, when it featured in Formula One's inaugural season. The venue has maintained continuous Grand Prix racing since 1985, aside from gaps in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve spans 4. 361 kilometers and serves as the permanent home of the Canadian Grand Prix in Formula One. Beyond its Formula One commitment, the track has accommodated various international racing series including sportscar championships and North American open-wheel competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport venue hosted the Formula One Chinese Grand Prix annually between 2004 and 2019, with the race resuming from 2024. The circuit has expanded its motorsport calendar to include electric racing competitions alongside the Grand Prix.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone in Northamptonshire, this English circuit inaugurated the British Grand Prix in 1948 and hosted the inaugural Formula One World Championship race two years later. After sharing the British Grand Prix with rival venues between 1955 and 1986, the event became a permanent fixture at this track from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest became a historic venue when it hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held in Eastern Europe in 1986, just three years after construction began on the 4. 381 km circuit. Built in merely eight months, faster than any comparable Formula One track, the venue was developed outside the city as an alternative to an initially proposed street circuit in Budapest's central park.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km Italian racing venue constructed in 1922 near Milan, ranking as the third purpose-built motorsport circuit globally and Europe's oldest on the mainland. Home to the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, the track has earned its nickname "the Temple of Speed" for its distinctive long straights and rapid cornering sections that enable consistently high velocities.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue in Mie Prefecture operated by Honda Mobilityland, featuring a capacity of 155,000 spectators. The track gained prominence as a regular Formula One Grand Prix host and also stages Japanese Super Formula competitions.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, weaving around the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its collection of major hotels and casinos. The layout incorporates several of the city's most recognizable landmarks, such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: This 4. 304 km Mexico City circuit is named after two Mexican racing brothers killed in separate accidents during the 1960s and early 1970s. The venue has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix across three distinct eras, most recently from 2015 onwards under its current Mexico City Grand Prix designation, though on a different configuration than during its previous hosting periods that ended in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary racing facility constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Florida, measuring 3. 363 miles with 19 corners and supporting average qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Created by specialist track designers Apex Circuit Design, the circuit joined the Formula One calendar in 2022 as the venue for the Miami Grand Prix.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street layout running through Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, encompassing the harbourfront area of the Principality. It is widely known as the Monte Carlo circuit due to the majority of its course being situated within the Monte Carlo quarter.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Situated in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km layout that resumed hosting Formula One in 2021 with the revival of the Dutch Grand Prix, though this arrangement concludes following the 2026 season. The venue, currently bearing a three-year naming rights agreement from July 2025, represents a return to the championship after decades away.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Lusail International Circuit, situated north of Doha in Qatar, is a 5. 419-kilometre racing venue featuring a 1. 068-kilometre main straight and holding an FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309-kilometer circuit in São Paulo, Brazil, opened in 1940 and renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The counterclockwise track hosts major racing events and features an adjacent kart facility honoring fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront, serving as the permanent home of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix in Formula One since its inaugural running in 2021. The track has also begun hosting international electric racing events from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Marina Bay area, incorporating sections of the Downtown Core and Kallang districts in its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of lengthy straightaways and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for all racing disciplines. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas spans 3. 426 miles and meets FIA Grade 1 standards for international motorsport competition. The venue serves as the primary American venue for Formula One's world championship, while also hosting major events in MotoGP, NASCAR, and sports car racing including the Lone Star Le Mans endurance competition.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon, a dual Thai and British national, represents Thailand on the Formula One grid as a driver for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he secured back-to-back world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006, accumulating 32 race victories across 23 seasons. Beyond Formula One, Alonso achieved historic success in endurance racing, winning the 2018–19 World Endurance Championship and two Le Mans 24 Hours victories with Toyota, establishing himself as the sole driver to win both a Formula One world title and the World Endurance Drivers' Championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli represents Italy in Formula One, currently driving for Mercedes. Since entering the championship in 2025, the driver has secured six Grand Prix victories.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, competing at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One as part of the Audi team.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 13-season career that includes 10 Grand Prix victories. He achieved runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during consecutive years with Mercedes, finishing second in both 2019 and 2020.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently racing in Formula One for the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan balances his endurance racing commitments in European Le Mans Series with a reserve role at Haas in Formula One, having made seven Grand Prix appearances between 2024 and 2025.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The driver achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a racing driver with French and Algerian heritage who currently races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, competing under the French flag.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding an unprecedented seven world championship titles alongside Michael Schumacher. The accomplished driver also maintains multiple all-time records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg, a German driver, currently races for Audi in Formula One. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he has achieved success in endurance motorsport, notably securing victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 alongside Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Racing Bulls.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc is a Monégasque driver competing for Ferrari in Formula One. He finished as championship runner-up in 2022 and has claimed nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in the sport.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver who has competed in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and 2022-2024. Currently, he races in the World Endurance Championship as a BMW factory driver for WRT, while also undertaking part-time NASCAR competition with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently racing for McLaren, secured the Formula One World Drivers' Championship in 2025. Over his eight-season career, he has accumulated 12 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The versatile competitor previously secured a victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez, a Mexican driver currently racing for Cadillac, finished second in the 2023 championship standings during his tenure with Red Bull. Across his 15-year Formula One career, he has secured six Grand Prix victories.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver, races for McLaren in Formula One and has secured nine Grand Prix victories during his four-season tenure in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger", competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell is a British Formula One driver currently competing for Mercedes who has claimed seven race victories during his eight-year tenure in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Carlos Sainz is a Spanish Formula One driver currently racing for Williams who has claimed four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-year career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American racing driver who competed in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons. Currently, he races in the World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category for Proton Competition, having previously driven in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin in the sport's premier championship.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda competed in Formula One between 2021 and 2025, currently holding a reserve position with both Red Bull Racing and its sister team Racing Bulls.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver competes for Red Bull Racing and has secured four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12 seasons in Formula One, Verstappen has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu holds the distinction of being the sole Chinese driver to have competed in Formula One, with an active racing presence from 2022 through 2024. He currently fulfills a reserve driver role for the Cadillac team in the sport.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed as Alpine since 2021, following its rebranding from the Renault F1 Team to promote the French manufacturer's sports car division. Operating as Renault's official works team until the company's 2025 departure from the sport, Alpine secured a single victory through Esteban Ocon at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix and currently powers its cars with Mercedes engines.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin is a British automotive manufacturer that has engaged in Formula One competition through different organizational structures, with its present incarnation operating as a works team competing under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian automaker, stands as Formula One's longest-established and most accomplished team, participating continuously in the world championship since its inception in 1950. The squad, nicknamed after their emblematic logo, has maintained an unbroken presence throughout the sport's entire history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas established this American-licensed Formula One team in 2014, and it competed for the first time in 2016. The organization changed leadership in early 2024 when Ayao Komatsu took over as team principal, succeeding Guenther Steiner who had held the position since the team's foundation.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Established in 1970 by Peter Sauber as an engineering and racing operation, this Swiss constructor initially found success in endurance competition, including a Le Mans victory in 1989. The team competed in Formula One from 1993 onwards as an independent manufacturer before being acquired by Audi in 2024, concluding its tenure as one of the sport's longest-serving constructors.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its state-of-the-art facility in Woking. The racing team operates as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group, with full ownership held by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has been a significant force in Formula One since 1954, operating as both a constructor and engine supplier at different times. The current Mercedes-AMG Petronas team, based in Brackley and holding a German licence, has been jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Toto Wolff, and Ineos since January 2022. The team is historically known by the "Silver Arrows" moniker, reflecting its German racing heritage.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024 as one of two Red Bull-owned outfits in the sport. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the team operates alongside its sister squad Red Bull Racing under the Austrian conglomerate's ownership structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced competition in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team operation. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the team functions as a sister outfit to Red Bull Racing within the Austrian conglomerate's motorsport portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing operates as an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England and owned by Red Bull GmbH since its 2005 establishment. Under Christian Horner's leadership through 2024, the team competed at the sport's highest level before Horner's departure led to Laurent Mekies assuming the management role.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding an earlier failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team designation and operates from a substantial purpose-built facility.
